title: Silent reserve drain due to burst-gating heuristic — hotfix & postmortem
creator: Liam Chen
description: Summary: An autoscaler change that added a conservative burst-gating heuristic caused gradual, opaque depletion of reserved pool headroom for multi-tenant Dedicated clusters. Several customers experienced elevated 429s and long tail latency during weekday peak windows. This ticket tracks the detection, emergency mitigation, hotfix rollout, root cause analysis, and follow-up engineering work.

root_cause: The new burst-gating heuristic introduced in autoscaler v2.11 incorrectly applied a per-tenant gating multiplier when evaluating available headroom. For low-cardinality tenants that frequently acquire short-duration microbursts, the multiplier made the autoscaler classify pool headroom as ‘constrained’ too early, which suppressed transient scale-ups and allowed smaller, frequent allocations to consume available reserved capacity without triggering replenishment. Additionally, telemetry aggregation reduced visibility into short-lived slot churn, delaying detection.
mitigation: 1) Immediate revert of the gating multiplier change (rollback of v2.11) on 2026-03-08; 2) Temporary burst-backfill service enabled to allocate replenishment credits for affected tenants; 3) Emergency scaling window widened from 30s to 90s for high-priority tenants while we validated the fix.
fix_summary: Merged hotfix that: (a) restores original multiplier semantics in the gating decision; (b) adds an explicit microburst-aware headroom estimator that uses rolling 1m and 5m windowed quantiles instead of a single aggregated instant; (c) emits per-tenant microburst metrics to the telemetry pipeline; (d) adds an autoscaler safety net that triggers a forced replenishment if reserved pool headroom drops below 8% for more than two consecutive windows. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/13496
rollout: Canary rollout started 2026-03-09 02:40 UTC to 3% of dedicated clusters, observed for 8 hours; no regressions seen. Gradual ramp to 100% completed by 2026-03-09 11:00 UTC with monitoring checks at 5, 30, 60 minutes. Post-rollout, we left safety net enabled and monitored for 72 hours before de-escalation.
verification:
- Telemetry: reserved-pool-headroom metric back within expected range across affected clusters
- Customer-reports: Medivault observed 95% reduction in 429s within 20 minutes of rollback
- Load tests: synthetic microburst workload replayed against staging confirmed autoscaler responds within target window and does not suppress necessary scale-ups
- Dashboards: added dedicated 'microburst headroom' chart and alert with 5-min aggregation threshold
